about: Sourced life stories for the first men of Genesis (Adam, Noah, Heth, Javan), Aaron, Eleazar and the three sons of Levi. Written from the KJV text itself; no reviewed dossier exists for these people.

adam-gen-2-19.short: The first man in Genesis, formed from the dust, who named the animals, ate of the forbidden tree with Eve, and was sent out of Eden.

paragraphs.text: Genesis tells of the making of man twice. In the first account God said, "Let us make man in our image", created them male and female on the sixth day, blessed them and gave them dominion over the living creatures. In the second, the LORD God "formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life", and put him in a garden eastward in Eden "to dress it and to keep it". The book of Adam's generations in chapter 5 says that God made him "in the likeness of God" and "called their name Adam".

The LORD God told the man he might eat of every tree of the garden except the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, "for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die." He brought the beasts and the birds to Adam to see what he would call them, and whatever Adam called each one, "that was the name thereof"; but no help meet was found for him. So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, took one of his ribs and made a woman, and Adam said, "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh".

The serpent persuaded the woman to eat of the forbidden tree, and she gave also to her husband, "and he did eat." When the LORD God called, "Where art thou?", Adam said he had hidden because he was naked, and answered, "The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree". The LORD God told him the ground was cursed for his sake and that he would eat bread in the sweat of his face, "for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return." Adam named his wife Eve, "because she was the mother of all living"; the LORD God made them coats of skins, sent him out of the garden, and set Cherubims and a flaming sword to keep the way of the tree of life.

Adam and Eve's first sons were Cain, a tiller of the ground, and Abel, a keeper of sheep, and Cain killed Abel. Then Eve bore Seth, saying God had appointed her "another seed instead of Abel". Genesis 5 says Adam was a hundred and thirty years old when Seth was born, that he had other sons and daughters, and that "all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died."

Luke's genealogy of Jesus ends with "the son of Adam, which was the son of God." Paul writes that "death reigned from Adam to Moses" and calls Adam "the figure of him that was to come". To the Corinthians he writes, "as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive", and sets "The first man Adam" beside "the last Adam". In the first letter to Timothy Paul writes that "Adam was first formed, then Eve."

noah-gen-5-29.short: Son of Lamech who found grace in the eyes of the LORD, built the ark, came through the flood with his family, and received God's covenant of the bow.

paragraphs.text: Noah was the son of Lamech, who named him saying, "This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed." When Noah was five hundred years old he had three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth. Genesis does not name his wife. In a time when God saw that the wickedness of man was great, "Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD"; he was "a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God."

God told Noah that the earth was filled with violence and that he would destroy all flesh with the earth. He told him to make an ark of gopher wood, three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits broad and thirty cubits high, with a window, a door in the side, and three stories. Noah was to bring in two of every sort, male and female, and food for them all; in chapter 7 the LORD also told him to take the clean beasts and the birds by sevens. "Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he."

Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came. In the second month, on the seventeenth day, Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives went into the ark with the animals, "and the LORD shut him in"; the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and it rained forty days and forty nights. The waters rose fifteen cubits upward and the mountains were covered; every living thing on the dry land died, "and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark." The waters prevailed on the earth a hundred and fifty days.

"God remembered Noah", and the waters went down. The ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day, upon the mountains of Ararat, and the tops of the mountains were seen on the first day of the tenth month. After forty days Noah opened the window and sent out a raven, then a dove, which came back; seven days later the dove returned with an olive leaf in her mouth, and after seven more days she did not return. On the first day of the first month of the six hundred and first year the waters were dried up, and when the earth was dry, on the twenty-seventh day of the second month, God told Noah to go out of the ark with his family and every living thing.

Noah built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean bird, and the LORD said he would not again curse the ground for man's sake. God blessed Noah and his sons, telling them, "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth." He made a covenant with them and with every living creature that there would not be a flood to destroy the earth again, and set his bow in the cloud as "the token of the covenant".

Noah became a husbandman and planted a vineyard; he drank of the wine, was drunken, and lay uncovered in his tent. Ham saw and told his brothers, and Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father. When Noah awoke he said, "Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren", and blessed "the LORD God of Shem". He lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood, and "all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years: and he died." Ezekiel later names him with Daniel and Job, in Matthew Jesus spoke of "the days of Noe", and Hebrews says that "By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house".

heth-gen-10-15.short: A son of Canaan named only in two genealogies; most verses on his record speak of the children of Heth, the people from whom Abraham bought a burial cave.

paragraphs.text: Heth is named as a man in only two places, the table of nations in Genesis and its repeat in Chronicles: "Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth". Canaan was a son of Ham, the son of Noah. Scripture tells nothing else about Heth himself: no wife, no deeds and no death.

Most verses on this record do not speak of the man but of a people: "the sons of Heth" or "the children of Heth", and the Hittites, whom the record gathers under the same name. Abraham bought the field and cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite "in the audience of the children of Heth", and Rebekah said she was weary of her life "because of the daughters of Heth".

javan-gen-10-2.short: A son of Japheth named in two genealogies with his four sons; most verses on his record speak of a people, not of the man.

paragraphs.text: Javan is named among the seven sons of Japheth, the son of Noah, in Genesis 10 and again in 1 Chronicles 1. Four sons are listed for him: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim. Genesis adds of these families that by them "were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands". Scripture tells nothing else about the man himself.

Most verses on this record speak of a people rather than the man: Joel's "Grecians" and the "Greeks" and "Grecians" of the New Testament, which the record gathers under his name. Isaiah also names Javan among the nations, with "the isles afar off", and Ezekiel names Javan among the traders of Tyrus. Scripture itself does not say that the Greeks descended from him.

aaron-exo-4-14.short: Moses' brother and spokesman before Pharaoh, who made the golden calf, was anointed priest with his sons, and died on mount Hor.

paragraphs.text: Aaron was a Levite, the son of Amram and Jochebed, and the brother of Moses and Miriam. He married Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Naashon, and she bore him four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. When Moses told the LORD that he was "slow of speech", the LORD said of Aaron, "I know that he can speak well", and made him Moses' spokesman to the people. Aaron went into the wilderness, met Moses at the mount of God and kissed him; then he spoke the LORD's words to the elders of Israel and did the signs before them, and the people believed.

Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said, "Let my people go"; Exodus gives Moses' age then as eighty and Aaron's as eighty-three. The LORD told Moses, "Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet." Before Pharaoh Aaron cast down his rod and it became a serpent, and when the magicians did the same, "Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods." The LORD told Moses to have Aaron stretch out his rod over the waters of Egypt, and the river was turned to blood; Aaron then stretched out his hand over the waters and the frogs came up, and when he struck the dust with his rod it became lice. The magicians could not bring forth lice, and said, "This is the finger of God".

When Moses went up the mount to receive the tables of stone, he left Aaron and Hur with the elders. The people, saying they did not know what had become of Moses, gathered to Aaron: "Up, make us gods, which shall go before us". Aaron asked for their golden earrings, fashioned a molten calf with a graving tool, built an altar before it and proclaimed, "To morrow is a feast to the LORD." When Moses came down and asked what the people had done to him, Aaron answered, "thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief", and said of the gold, "I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf." Deuteronomy records Moses saying that the LORD was very angry with Aaron, and that he prayed for Aaron too.

The LORD told Moses to take Aaron and his sons "that he may minister unto me in the priest's office", and to make Aaron holy garments "for glory and for beauty". Moses washed Aaron and his sons, clothed Aaron with the coat, the robe, the ephod and the breastplate with the Urim and the Thummim, set the mitre with its golden plate on his head, and poured the anointing oil on his head. For seven days Aaron and his sons stayed at the door of the tabernacle. Then Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the offering on the altar.

Then his sons Nadab and Abihu offered "strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not", and fire went out from the LORD and devoured them. Moses told Aaron that the LORD would be sanctified in them that come near him, "And Aaron held his peace." Aaron and his other sons were told not to uncover their heads or tear their clothes, nor to go out from the door of the tabernacle. When Moses was angry that the sin offering had been burnt and not eaten, Aaron answered that "such things have befallen me" that day, and Moses "was content". Nadab and Abihu had no children, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests "in the sight of Aaron their father".

Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married, asking, "hath he not spoken also by us?" The LORD called the three of them out to the tabernacle, spoke to Aaron and Miriam of his servant Moses, and when the cloud departed Miriam was leprous. Aaron said to Moses, "Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly", and Moses cried to God for her. She was shut out of the camp seven days.

Korah and his company rose against Moses and Aaron, saying, "Ye take too much upon you", and when the whole congregation later murmured against them, a plague began. At Moses' word Aaron took a censer with fire from the altar, ran into the midst of the congregation and made an atonement; "he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed." Then twelve rods were laid up before the LORD, with Aaron's name written on the rod of Levi, and the next day his rod had "brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds." It was kept before the testimony as a token against the rebels, and Hebrews names "Aaron's rod that budded" among the things in the ark of the covenant.

At Kadesh, where Miriam died, there was no water, and the LORD told Moses and Aaron to speak to the rock; Moses struck it twice with his rod. The LORD said to them both, "Because ye believed me not", they would not bring the congregation into the land; this was "the water of Meribah". At mount Hor, by the land of Edom, Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there on the top of the mount; Numbers gives his age as a hundred and twenty-three, and all Israel mourned him thirty days. Deuteronomy, in a list of Israel's journeys, says: "to Mosera: there Aaron died, and there he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead."

eleazar-exo-6-23.short: Aaron's son, who served as priest in his father's lifetime, received his garments on mount Hor, and with Joshua divided the land by lot.

paragraphs.text: Eleazar was the third-named of the four sons of Aaron and Elisheba. He married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. With his father and brothers he was taken to minister in the priest's office, and Moses washed and clothed them.

When fire from the LORD devoured his brothers Nadab and Abihu, Moses told Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar not to uncover their heads or tear their clothes. Later that day Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar because the sin offering had been burnt and not eaten, until Aaron answered him. Nadab and Abihu had no children, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests "in the sight of Aaron their father".

Eleazar was made "chief over the chief of the Levites", with charge of the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the daily meat offering and the anointing oil. After Korah's rebellion he took up the brasen censers of the men who had been burnt, and they were made into broad plates to cover the altar. The red heifer was to be given to him, brought outside the camp and slain before him. On mount Hor Moses put Aaron's garments on Eleazar, and after Aaron died, Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount; Deuteronomy says that "Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead."

In the plains of Moab Eleazar numbered the people with Moses, and the daughters of Zelophehad stood before them both with their request. His son Phinehas went with the army to the war against Midian, and Eleazar received the spoil with Moses and told the soldiers how to purify it. Moses set Joshua before Eleazar, and the LORD said Joshua would stand before Eleazar, who would ask counsel for him "after the judgment of Urim before the LORD".

Eleazar and Joshua were named to divide the land, and with the heads of the tribes they gave out the inheritances by lot in Shiloh. Eleazar died and was buried in a hill in mount Ephraim that belonged to Phinehas his son. Chronicles traces the priests' line from him through Phinehas to Zadok and on to Jehozadak, who went into captivity, and Ezra's own line runs back to "Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest".

kohath-gen-46-11.short: Son of Levi who went down to Egypt with Jacob, grandfather of Aaron, Moses and Miriam, and father of the Kohathites, who carried the holy things.

paragraphs.text: Kohath was one of the three sons of Levi, Gershon, Kohath and Merari, who went down into Egypt with Jacob's household. His sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, and Exodus says "the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years." Scripture tells nothing of his own deeds.

Through his son Amram he was the grandfather of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Amram married Jochebed, whom Exodus calls "his father's sister" and Numbers "the daughter of Levi". Korah, who rose against Moses and Aaron, was "the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath", and Chronicles traces the singer Heman back to Kohath as well.

Most verses on this record speak of his descendants, the Kohathites, not of the man. In the wilderness they camped on the south side of the tabernacle and, after Aaron and his sons had covered the ark and the holy vessels, carried them on their shoulders. In the land, the sons of Aaron among them had the first lot of cities.

gershon-gen-46-11.short: First-named of Levi's three sons, spelled Gershon and, in Chronicles, also Gershom; father of Libni and Shimei, and of the Gershonite Levites.

paragraphs.text: Gershon is named first among the three sons of Levi who went down into Egypt with Jacob. The KJV spells his name Gershon in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers and Joshua, and both Gershon and Gershom in Chronicles. His sons were Libni and Shimi, spelled Shimei in Numbers and Chronicles. Scripture tells nothing of his own deeds.

Most verses on this record speak of his descendants, the Gershonites, not of the man. In the wilderness they camped behind the tabernacle westward and carried its curtains, coverings and hangings, with two wagons and four oxen, under Ithamar the son of Aaron. In the land they received thirteen cities by lot, Golan in Bashan among them.

merari-gen-46-11.short: Third-named son of Levi, who went down to Egypt with Jacob; father of Mahli and Mushi, and of the Merarite Levites.

paragraphs.text: Merari is named third among the sons of Levi who went down into Egypt with Jacob. His sons were Mahli and Mushi; Exodus spells the first Mahali, and Chronicles also names sons of Merari "by Jaaziah". Scripture tells nothing of his own deeds.

Most verses on this record speak of his descendants, the Merarites, not of the man. In the wilderness they camped on the north side of the tabernacle and carried its boards, bars, pillars and sockets, with four wagons and eight oxen, under Ithamar the son of Aaron. In the land they received twelve cities out of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun, and Chronicles names Ethan of the sons of Merari among David's singers.
